brief: The Fed hiked 25bps to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike since 2023, with a unanimous vote and a hawkish dot plot showing 16 of 18 officials expecting further tightening this year. Markets responded by pricing roughly 75bps more by next June and about 50% odds of an October hike, pushing 2yr yields to a 2-year high of 4.74% and 10yr yields to a post-2007 high of 5.02%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.45% led by banks and energy shares. DB's US economists now expect another 50bps via December and March hikes. Equity losses were cushioned by an oil pullback after Saudi Arabia signaled faster pipeline repairs and increased tanker loadings, and after Libya restored output. In the UK, CPI printed in line with consensus, pulling BoE surprise-hike odds down to 9% from 23%; DB's UK economists still expect a hold. Separately, US retail sales beat sharply, lifting Atlanta Fed GDPNow to +5.1% for Q3, even as the NAHB housing index fell to a 12-month low.
